learning_objective: The learner will infer what a screen reader typically announces for each of six snippets of page markup, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** screen-reader-announcement-matcher
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** infer
**Learning Objective:** The learner will infer what a screen reader typically announces for each of six snippets of page markup, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Screen Reader, Alt Text, Decorative Image, Heading Structure (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each snippet the learner commits one of three announcements before the answer is shown. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct announcement column in Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Reading the worked-example table is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A screen reader describes what an image looks like by itself. (2) An image with no alt attribute is skipped. (3) A heading is read as ordinary text. **Instructional Rationale:** Inferring the announcement from the markup is an Understand-level action that connects what an author writes to what a listener hears. Six snippets that differ in one detail each teach the learner to read markup as a listener would. **Content:** The sim states that announcements are typical and simplified, and that wording differs between screen readers. The six snippets: | # | Snippet shown to the learner | Option A | Option B | Option C | Correct | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | A heading "How water moves" at level 2 | Heading level 2, How water moves | How water moves | Link, How water moves | A | A heading is announced with its level. | | 2 | An image with alt text "A river meandering through a valley" | Image, river dot png | Image, A river meandering through a valley | Nothing | B | The alt text is read as the image's description. | | 3 | An image with no alt attribute and the file name river.png | Image, river dot png | Image, a river | Nothing | A | Without alt text, the file name is often read. | | 4 | An image with an empty alt attribute | Image, no description | Image, decorative | Nothing | C | An empty alt attribute tells the reader to skip the image. | | 5 | A link whose text is "click here" | Link, click here | Link, goes to the runoff page | Button, click here | A | The reader announces only the link text, which says nothing about the destination. | | 6 | A button that contains only an image with no alt text, file name close.png | Button, close dot png | Button, close | Nothing | A | The file name becomes the button's name, which is useless. | **Provenance:** The snippets are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The announcements are typical and simplified, and the sim states that they vary between programs. **Rules:** Each snippet has exactly one correct option, in the position shown in the Correct column. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one snippet and three options. 2. The learner chooses an option, and the choice is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After snippet 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 snippets in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [announcement]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. A screen reader typically says: [announcement]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can hear the markup." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed snippet. **Starting State:** The first snippet and its three options. The question shown is "What does a screen reader typically say?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's worked example lists four snippets and what a screen reader typically says: a heading with its level, an image with alt text, an image with no alt attribute read as its file name, and an image with empty alt text skipped.
